data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The night-time UHI is dominated by stored sensible heat: urban masonry and asphalt absorb daytime solar radiation and, having high thermal mass and heat capacity, release it as longwave radiation and sensible heat after sunset, while the sky-view factor (SVF) of dense street canyons traps that longwave emission, slowing nocturnal cooling; cross-city, the gap scales with built density (building height / street width) because a lower SVF increasingly retards radiative cooling.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If measurements show rural and urban surfaces have identical cooling rates in the first three hours after sunset, the storage-release mechanism is not the dominant cause.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the cross-city UHI gap does not correlate with sky-view factor or built density once population/anthropogenic heat is controlled, the SVF-trapping explanation for cross-city variation fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the nocturnal UHI vanishes on overcast nights with low wind (which suppress radiative cooling but do not remove stored heat), the SVF-longwave mechanism is disfavored relative to, e.g., anthropogenic heat.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the UHI is already fully developed immediately at sunset with no temporal growth, delayed storage release is not the principal driver.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"During the day, impervious, low-albedo urban surfaces with high thermal mass and heat capacity integrate solar input into a subsurface heat reservoir. After sunset, when the surface energy balance is dominated by radiative cooling and the sensible heat flux turns downward, this stored heat is conducted back to the surface and radiated away as longwave. In a dense street canyon, the sky view factor is small, so a large fraction of the emitted longwave intercepts building walls rather than escaping to the cold sky; walls re-absorb and re-emit, recycling energy and sustaining surface and air temperature. The lower the SVF, the slower the nocturnal cooling rate, so the temperature excess over open countryside (SVF \u2248 1) persists and grows through the night. The magnitude of the effect depends on how much heat was stored (thermal mass \u00d7 insolation) and how efficiently it is trapped (SVF).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
